newsitem.title: UK: UK's Darling-rate rise due to previous government.
newsitem.headline: UK's Darling-rate rise due to previous government.

text.p: Britain's Labour government on Thursday said economic mismanagement by the previous Conservative administration led to the latest quarter point rate rise.

"What you are seeing at the moment is the consequence of a failure to take action on interest rate policy over a year ago," Alistair Darling, chief secretary to the Treasury and number two to Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown, told BBC Radio in an interview.
The Bank of England raised rates to 6.75 percent from 6.5 percent, the third rate rise in as many months.
Darling said he was "well aware" of the problems faced by exporters due to the strong pound, but said the government had no options but to sanction tough action.
"It was necessary for the new government to take some firm action and not to follow the last government which ducked all these hard decisions," he said.
